root_cause.text: The driver's command validation logic for NPU_OP_RESIZE uses a WARN_ON(1) placeholder that does not reject the command, allowing userspace to trigger a kernel warning on every submission, leading to log spam and a panic-based denial of service when panic_on_warn is enabled.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explains that "NPU_OP_RESIZE is a U85-only command that the driver does not yet implement. The existing WARN_ON(1) placeholder fires unconditionally whenever userspace submits this command ... causing unbounded kernel log spam. If panic_on_warn is set the kernel panics, giving any unprivileged user with access to the DRM device a trivial denial-of-service primitive." The patch diff shows the change from `WARN_ON(1); break;` to `return -EINVAL;`, which rejects the command before reaching hardware.

vuln_statements.explanation: Case label for NPU_OP_RESIZE; the command is not properly rejected, serving as the entry point for the vulnerable code path.
Placeholder call that triggers a kernel warning instead of returning an error, allowing userspace to cause log spam and panic when panic_on_warn is set.
Break statement after WARN_ON(1) that exits the switch without returning an error, failing to reject the invalid command.
Switch statement that dispatches based on command opcode; the absence of a proper error return for NPU_OP_RESIZE is the root cause.
Default case (if present) might also be relevant; if not handled, other invalid commands could similarly bypass validation.
